independent_variables.definition: The Table 6 row is labeled UNA1; the paper’s variable definitions call the proxy UNA. UNA is the in-sample rank of negative verifiable net assets (VNA), where VNA is [cash plus all investments and advances, less debt and preferred equity] divided by [assets less liabilities]. The negative rank increases with the unverifiability of net assets.
independent_variables.formula: in_sample_rank(−[(cash + all investments and advances − debt − preferred equity) / (assets − liabilities)])

evidence.quote: UNA: We compute the ratio of [cash ? all investments and advances - debt preferred equity] to [assets - liabilities]. The denominator in this ratio is total net assets, while the numerator is intended to proxy for that component of net assets whose fair-values are likely most verifiable (Richardson et al. 2005). Thus this ratio is intended to capture the verifiability of net assets (VNA). Items excluded from the numerator include plant and equipment, receivables, payables, inventories, advances, etc. Fair-value estimates of these items are likely less verifiable than cash, investments, debt, and preferred equity. Thus as the VNA ratio decreases, subjectivity in estimating the fair value of goodwill is expected to increase. To obtain a measure that increases in the subjectivity of estimating the fair value of goodwill, we multiply VNA by -1. We then rank the resulting value in-sample and denote it UNA, where ‘‘UNA’’ refers to the unverifiability of net assets.

evidence.quote: UNA: We compute the ratio of [cash ? all investments and advances - debt preferred equity] to [assets - liabilities]. The denominator in this ratio is total net assets, while the numerator is intended to proxy for that component of net assets whose fair-values are likely most verifiable (Richardson et al. 2005). Thus this ratio is intended to capture the verifiability of net assets (VNA). Items excluded from the numerator include plant and equipment, receivables, payables, inventories, advances, etc. Fair-value estimates of these items are likely less verifiable than cash, investments, debt, and preferred equity. Thus as the VNA ratio decreases, subjectivity in estimating the fair value of goodwill is expected to increase. To obtain a measure that increases in the subjectivity of estimating the fair value of goodwill, we multiply VNA by -1. We then rank the resulting value in-sample and denote it UNA, where ‘‘UNA’’ refers to the unverifiability of net assets.
